Lenore — thanks for the matrix and constraints. Quick read: traffic shape matches the earlier signals. We ran a validation pass against your sample and produced an updated sizing recommendation (attached: skybridge_sizing_report_v3.xlsx) and a mutual action plan (attached: mutual_action_plan_Skybridge_v4.pdf). High-level callouts: 

- Baseline capacity: 12 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (4 pods of 3 GPUs) for steady-state to hit 400k tokens/s sustained with <60ms p50 token latency on recommended model family.
- Burst buffer: Autoscaler configured to add +4 GPUs for burst windows (expected up to 1.8x traffic).
- Safety headroom: +20% for model variability and rare peak patterns.
- KV warming: we recommend a pre-cutover warm period of 48 hours with traffic mirror at 10% to ensure prefix caching and KV hit-rate >= 85%.

Acceptance tests we’ll run in staging prior to cutover:
- Sustained throughput run (3 hours) at 1.2x expected steady-state with latency and error-rate monitoring.
- End-to-end request tracing and tail latency profiling (p95/p99).
- Failover/rollback exercise (simulated degraded GPU and network leaf failure).

Proposed cutover window: May 22 20:00 PDT – May 23 06:00 PDT (8 hours main window + 2-hour verification). The window assumes Skybridge procurement and ops have approved DB/network change freeze and token-rate throttles.

Open questions where we need your sign-off by May 14:
1) Approval of baseline GPU count + burst policy.
2) Acceptance-test owners (who from Skybridge runs the mirror traffic and signs off on KV hit target).
3) Procurement timeline for DocuSign and any early invoicing exceptions.

We also dropped a draft cutover runbook in the repo (cutover-runbook-draft.md). Please flag anything missing.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Quick technical confirmation from my side — did a short performance sweep against the Skybridge sample with the recommended model config and quantization profile. Notes: 

- With 12x A100-80GB equiv (4 pods x3) we see ~420k tokens/s sustained using our batching profile; p95 token latency ~180ms when clients respect a 60s max context and 8-12 token generation windows.
- Autoscaler must be tuned for concurrency (scale-by-rps) rather than GPU utilization alone; otherwise we see slow spin-up during sudden bursts.
- KV-cache warm is critical — without a 48-hour mirror the first-24h production error-rate is +0.6% and latency spikes.

I recommend we add a pre-cutover dry-run on May 20 where Redwood will mirror 10% of traffic for a 6-hour window and share metrics. If that looks good we greenlight May 22 full swap.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
